counting_rules:
* A command line is split into pipeline stages on ``|``, ``|&``, ``;``, ``&&``, ``||``, ``&`` and
      newlines. ``$(...)``, backticks and ``<(...)``/``>(...)`` are parsed as further command lines.
    * The head of each stage is counted once. Leading ``VAR=value`` assignments and redirections are
      skipped. ``then``/``do``/``else``/``elif``/``!``/``{``/``(`` are skipped and the command after
      them is counted. ``if``/``while``/``until`` are counted and so is the command that follows
      (the condition). ``for``/``case``/``select`` are counted and the rest of the stage is ignored.
      ``fi``/``done``/``esac``/``}`` are not counted.
    * Wrappers in WRAPPERS (sudo, doas, env, xargs, time, nohup, nice, exec, command, builtin,
      timeout, watch) are counted, their own options are skipped, and the wrapped utility is counted
      too when one is present. ``find ... -exec/-execdir/-ok/-okdir CMD`` also counts CMD.
    * A head containing ``/`` is reduced to its basename, except ``./x``, ``../x`` and ``~/x`` which
      are counted as ``<./script>``. Heads that are not plain names (variables, ``-flags``, numbers,
      dotfiles, prompt residue such as ``user@host:~$``, ``diff`` output such as ``2c1``, globs) are
      not counted; they are reported as ``unparsed_stages``.
    * Within a source, commands below ``min_count = max(2, round(2e-6 * total_heads))`` are dropped
      from ``counts`` (the dropped mass is reported). Relative frequencies use the full total.

sources.title: NL2Bash corpus, data/bash/all.cm (Lin et al., LREC 2018)
sources.license: MIT for data/bash (data/bash/LICENSE and README: 'The dataset data/bash is separately licensed under MIT license'); the repository code is GPL-3.0
sources.note: One-liners collected from Q&A sites and tutorials and written by programmers to answer natural-language file-system/text tasks. Reflects what experts write to solve posed tasks, not what people type day to day. Heavily skewed towards find (and xargs/grep/-exec pipelines); interactive staples such as cd, git, vim, ssh are nearly absent.

sources.title: spignelon/bash_history (Hugging Face dataset, bash.txt)
sources.license: MIT as declared by the uploader in the dataset card; the card gives no provenance. The companion project (github.com/spignelon/CleverTerm, GPL-3.0) says the data came from the Kaggle dataset thuyngandao/bashlogs and from .bash_history files uploaded to GitHub and gists, whose original licenses are not documented
sources.note: Concatenated real interactive bash histories of an unknown number of (mostly Linux sysadmin/developer) users, one command line per line, repeats kept. Closest of the sources to day-to-day typing. Unknown deduplication, unknown per-user weighting (a few heavy users may dominate), some prompt/output residue lines (not counted).

combined_method: Unweighted mean over the 2 sources ['hf_bash_history', 'nl2bash'] of each command's relative frequency in that source (count / heads_counted, where heads_counted includes commands dropped below min_count; a command absent from a source contributes 0). Each source therefore weighs 1/2 regardless of size. Values are rounded to 8 decimals and sum to slightly less than 1. Restricted-licence sources are never included.
pipeline_lengths_method: Per command line that yielded at least one counted head: 1 + the number of top-level '|' or '|&' operators (pipes inside $(...)/backticks are not counted; lines joined by ';'/'&&' count the pipes of all their parts). Only sources made of raw command lines have it; the UCI token stream has no line boundaries and is omitted. pipeline_lengths_combined uses the same rule as combined: unweighted mean over ['hf_bash_history', 'nl2bash'] of each source's relative frequency.
